results.name: object_get_center_of_mass_and_scale
results.evidence: Copies three contiguous floats plus a trailing scalar from the object record (offsets 0xa0-0xac) into caller-supplied vector3d and scalar outputs, matching the usual center-of-mass+scale field grouping.
results.summary: Looks up an object by index (in_ECX) and copies its center-of-mass vector and a trailing scale/related scalar into the caller-supplied output pointers (in_EAX=vector3d*, param_1=scalar*).

results.name: object_initialize_shield_stun_thresholds
results.evidence: Reads fallback threshold values from the object's linked type block (fields at +8/+0xcc via the +0x7c reference), lets unaff_ESI/EDI override them, then writes obj[0x36]/[0x37] and derives boolean-style flags (0/1.0f) into obj[0x38]/[0x39] from their signs.
results.summary: Sets a pair of vitality-threshold fields on an object (with optional per-call overrides) and stores two derived boolean-style flags based on whether each threshold is positive.

results.name: object_update_vitality_and_regeneration
results.evidence: Per-tick object routine that manipulates the same shield-fraction (0x39) and health/shield flicker timers (0x3a-0x3e, 0x40, 0x41) used by object_apply_shield_damage/object_apply_body_damage; on an out-of-bounds/crush condition it builds a damage_data via damage_data_initialize and calls object_apply_damage (chimera__apply_damage) against itself.
results.summary: Advances an object's shield/health regeneration counters and stun flags each tick, and includes an instant-kill path (via a self-targeted object_apply_damage call) for an out-of-bounds/crushed condition.

results.name: damage_data_initialize
results.evidence: Zeroes an 0x54-byte struct, stores a tag/definition id at offset 0, writes -1 sentinels into the causer-object/causer-player-style fields, and sets two multiplier fields to 1.0 -- the canonical damage_data reset seen right before object_apply_damage (chimera__apply_damage) is invoked from object_update_vitality_and_regeneration.
results.summary: Clears and initializes a damage_data record (damage definition id, -1 causer sentinels, 1.0 multipliers) in the EDX-pointed buffer before it is passed to the apply-damage code.

results.name: object_health_force_full_when_unflagged
results.evidence: Guarded by status-word bit 0x4 (obj+0x106); when clear and the health fraction at obj+0xe0 is below 1.0, resets it to 1.0 and sets the 'changed' bit obj+0x10 |= 0x4000000, returning a status code built from floating compares.
results.summary: If an object's health-frozen status bit is clear and its health fraction is below full, restores full health and marks the object as changed.

results.name: object_clear_stun_and_wake_children
results.evidence: Guarded by status bit 0x4 on obj+0x106; when clear, notifies via FUN_004507a0 if the object's linked type object exists, and for vehicle-kind objects (obj[0x2d]==1) walks the child chain (obj+0x46/+0x114) flagging eligible children with bit 0x20, then forwards to object_clear_stationary_flag.
results.summary: Clears an object's stun bit, notifies any linked object, flags eligible seated/attached children, and forwards to the related sleep-clearing routine.

results.name: object_clear_stationary_flag
results.evidence: Guarded by status byte bit 0x8 (obj+0x107); notifies via FUN_004507a0 when the object's linked type object is valid, sets the bit, resets counter obj[0x3a] to 0, and calls object_regions_reset_permutation_lock.
results.summary: Clears an object's stationary/asleep bit, resets an associated timer, and forwards to region-lock refresh code.

results.name: object_shield_recharge_start
results.evidence: Reads the shield fraction at obj+0xe4 with NaN-aware compares; when not already exactly at its prior value, sets stun-adjacent bit 0x10, seeds the shield fraction to a small default (0x3c23d70a, ~0.01) if it was zero, clears the flicker-seed field obj+0x104, and sets byte obj+0x122.
results.summary: Kicks off shield-regeneration bookkeeping: flags the object as recharging, seeds a minimum shield value when empty, and resets flicker state.

results.name: object_children_recurse_prune
results.evidence: Walks an object's first-child link (obj+0x118) then the sibling chain (obj+0x114), calling FUN_004f41d0 on each and recursing into itself (object_children_recurse_prune) whenever that call reports failure.
results.summary: Recursively walks an object's attachment hierarchy, recursing further into any child for which FUN_004f41d0 fails.

results.name: object_deactivate_and_detach
results.evidence: Fetches the object's type block, calls object_clear_stun_and_wake_children, notifies via FUN_004507a0 when the type has a valid linked object, recurses through children via object_children_recurse_prune, and dispatches to FUN_004f5aa0 or FUN_004f59d0 depending on obj+4 being 0 or 3.
results.summary: Tears down an object's active links: clears stun state, notifies any linked object, recurses through its children, and runs type-specific cleanup for lifecycle states 0 and 3.

results.name: damage_apply_area_effect
results.evidence: Collects up to 0x40 nearby candidate objects via FUN_004f6fe0, applies object_damage_apply_line_of_sight to each one, then finalizes the damage_data with FUN_004fff20.
results.summary: Applies an area-of-effect damage_data to every nearby object gathered by FUN_004f6fe0, then finalizes/cleans up the damage record.

results.name: object_damage_apply_line_of_sight
results.evidence: Computes the vector from the damage_data's origin to the candidate object's position, runs an occlusion/collision test (FUN_00505880 with magic id 0xc221) possibly along multiple offset rays for vehicle-kind targets, derives a falloff fraction, and on success calls object_apply_damage (chimera__apply_damage) on the target before recursing into its next-attachment link (obj+0x46).
results.summary: Performs a line-of-sight/occlusion test between a damage source and a candidate object, computes distance-based falloff, and recursively applies object damage to it and its attached objects when unobstructed.

results.name: object_get_controlling_player_index
results.evidence: Walks up an object's parent chain (obj+0x11c) validating each ancestor against the object table by salt and object-kind bitmask (1<<kind & 3, i.e. biped or vehicle) with a loaded type, then returns FUN_00474db0(ancestor) -- a player-index resolver used the same way elsewhere (e.g. compared against a damage_data's responsible-player field).
results.summary: Walks up an object's ancestor chain to find the nearest valid biped/vehicle and returns the player index controlling it, or -1 if none is found.

results.name: light_probe_refresh_conditional
results.evidence: When global flag DAT_00689481 is set and cached tick counter DAT_006b8a00 is stale relative to the current tick (*(DAT_006f1d6c+0xc)), calls FUN_0046be40(0) and updates the cached counter.
results.summary: Refreshes a cached lighting probe roughly once every couple of ticks by comparing a cached tick counter against the current tick.

results.name: object_notify_hud_pickup_message
results.evidence: Validates the target index against the DAT_0087a480 datum table and via FUN_004f6ec0(3)/status checks, then builds a small argument block and dispatches it through FUN_004ec940(...,0x32,...) and FUN_004e1930(1,&DAT_00871de0,...), the same network/UI event pattern used elsewhere in this module; otherwise falls back to light_probe_refresh_conditional.
results.summary: Validates a target object then queues a UI/network event (message type 0x32), falling back to a lighting-probe refresh when the pickup/target conditions are not met.

results.name: object_apply_charge_and_notify
results.evidence: Checks a linked type-block pointer via FUN_004ec590, resolves an index through PTR_DAT_00687130+0x28, then applies a floating value to a target's regeneration fields (0xf4/0xe8, clamped to 1.0) obtained via FUN_004f6ec0(3), optionally calling object_clear_stationary_flag, and finally dispatches FUN_00566de0.
results.summary: Applies an energy/charge value to a target object's shield-flicker fields and dispatches a follow-up event, gated by a lookup-table validity check.

results.name: object_apply_damage
results.evidence: 15 callers; orchestrates the whole apply-damage pipeline for an object and its ancestor/attachment chain -- builds the local_44[] ancestor list, calls object_apply_shield_damage and object_apply_body_damage (which in turn call object_destroy_region) per level, dispatches HUD/network notification via object_damage_notify_and_impulse, and recursively distributes damage across attached child objects (obj+0x46) for vehicle-kind objects. Internally named chimera__apply_damage by the input hints, which is not a real Blam identifier.
results.summary: Applies a damage_data record to an object and every object in its parent/attachment chain, distributing the damage across shields, health, per-region effects, and attached children.

results.name: object_hash_clear_flag_bit3
results.evidence: Walks a hash-bucket linked list rooted through DAT_0087a464/DAT_0087a468 (identical traversal to object_hash_set_flag_bit3) clearing status bit 0x8 in each visited object's byte at offset 0x107.
results.summary: Walks a hash-chain of objects keyed by an index and clears status bit 0x8 on each one visited.

results.name: object_hash_set_flag_bit3
results.evidence: Identical hash-bucket traversal to object_hash_clear_flag_bit3 (DAT_0087a464/DAT_0087a468) but ORs status bit 0x8 into each object's byte at offset 0x107 instead of clearing it.
results.summary: Walks the same hash-chain of objects and sets status bit 0x8 on each one (paired setter for object_hash_clear_flag_bit3).

results.name: object_apply_body_damage
results.evidence: Reads/writes the object's health fraction (obj+0xe0) against its cap (obj+0xd8), scales incoming damage by a random multiplier (FUN_0046fe70), loops the damage-definition's per-region reaction list calling object_destroy_region, notifies FUN_004507a0/object_deactivate_and_detach on death thresholds (param_5+0x94/+0xb8), and spawns an impact effect via damage_effect_new_at_location.
results.summary: Applies the body/health portion of a damage_data to an object, handling low/critical health thresholds, per-region destruction, and death/impact-effect spawning.

results.name: object_apply_shield_damage
results.evidence: Reads/writes the object's shield fraction (obj+0xe4) and recharge rate (obj+0xdc), computes how much incoming damage the shield absorbs versus how much passes through as body damage, updates flicker meters (0xe8/0xf4), and clears the object's shield-charging bit via object_clear_stationary_flag when the shield reaches zero.
results.summary: Applies the shield portion of a damage_data to an object, absorbing damage up to the shield's remaining capacity and returning the leftover for body damage.

results.name: object_queue_damage_network_event
results.evidence: Builds a small argument block from the caller's damage-related fields (looking up one via hash_table_get / FUN_004f05e0) and forwards it through FUN_004ec940(...,0x31,...) then FUN_004e1a80(1,&DAT_00871de0,...), the same network/UI dispatch pattern used by object_notify_hud_pickup_message.
results.summary: Packages a damage-related argument block into a network/UI event (type 0x31) and dispatches it.

results.name: object_apply_scaled_impulse
results.evidence: Validates the object via FUN_004ec590, resolves a local index through PTR_DAT_00687130+0x28, scales a direction vector (local_c/local_8/local_4) by a magnitude (local_10), and forwards it to FUN_004bd080, the same vector sink used elsewhere as a physics-impulse consumer.
results.summary: Validates a linked object then scales a direction vector by a magnitude and forwards it as a physics impulse.

results.name: object_damage_notify_and_impulse
results.evidence: Fetches the object and its type block, applies a knockback impulse through FUN_004bd080 scaled by the type's mass-like field (+0x20) and the responsible object's velocity (param_2), branches on object-kind (obj[0x2d]) to fire kind-specific reactions (FUN_00559fa0/FUN_00571cb0/FUN_004bef80), and for player-controlled objects forwards a HUD/network notice via FUN_0046ff00 or FUN_00474db0+FUN_00460200, finally calling FUN_005674a0.
results.summary: After damage lands, applies a knockback impulse, fires object-kind-specific reaction effects (e.g. biped stagger vs vehicle recoil), and forwards the event to HUD/network and post-damage handlers.

results.name: object_damage_notify_tail_stub
results.evidence: An 8-byte body that duplicates the shared HUD/network-notify-then-FUN_005674a0 epilogue also found at the end of object_damage_notify_and_impulse; it has no callers in this module and its inherited PDB name ('mdp_decode_stateless_iterated') describes network-decode logic that does not match this code, consistent with a linker-folded (ICF) duplicate of that epilogue.
results.summary: A zero-caller stub whose body is identical to the tail of object_damage_notify_and_impulse (HUD/network notify then post-damage dispatch); the inherited 'mdp_decode' name does not match the actual (non-decode) behavior.

results.name: object_damage_notify_case_light_kind0
results.evidence: Ghidra-labelled switch case (switchD_004efdc9::caseD_0) whose body exactly matches the kind==0/1 light-reaction branch of object_damage_notify_and_impulse's switch (FUN_00559fa0/FUN_00571cb0), followed by the same HUD/network-notify epilogue -- an outlined case block of that function rather than an independent routine.
results.summary: Outlined switch-case block (kind 0/1 reaction) belonging to object_damage_notify_and_impulse's dispatch, followed by the shared HUD/network-notify epilogue.

results.name: object_damage_notify_default_case
results.evidence: 8-caller-less function whose body matches a default/other-kind branch of the same switch as object_damage_notify_and_impulse (calls FUN_0056cc80/FUN_00571cb0) followed by the identical HUD/network-notify epilogue; its inherited PDB name ('mdp_decode_incremental_iterated') does not match this behavior, again consistent with ICF-style code folding.
results.summary: Outlined default-case block of object_damage_notify_and_impulse's kind-based dispatch, followed by the same shared HUD/network-notify epilogue; the inherited name does not match the code.

results.name: object_notify_forward
results.evidence: 20-byte body that does nothing but tail-call FUN_004507a0 with whatever registers the caller set up; used identically by object_update_vitality_and_regeneration and object_clear_stationary_flag right after modifying vitality fields.
results.summary: Thin wrapper that forwards to the object-changed notifier FUN_004507a0.

results.name: damage_effect_new_at_location
results.evidence: Matches the cea-pdb hint exactly: builds the literal string array {'normal','incident','negative incident','reflection','gravity'} used as damage_effect placement-type names, computes an incident/reflection basis from a surface normal or object velocity fallback, and dispatches to FUN_00450870 (5 placement variants) or FUN_00450980.
results.summary: Spawns a damage_effect at an impact location, computing normal/incident/negative-incident/reflection/gravity oriented placements relative to the surface or object velocity.

results.name: damage_effect_place_forward
results.evidence: 56-byte body whose only action is a tail-call into FUN_00450870, the same effect-placement routine invoked from within damage_effect_new_at_location; the inherited PDB name ('mdpi_encode') describes network encoding, which does not match this behavior.
results.summary: Thin wrapper forwarding to the damage-effect placement routine FUN_00450870; despite its inherited name it performs no encoding.

results.name: object_destroy_region
results.evidence: Matches the cea-pdb hint via the '~damaged' string; guards against re-triggering a region via a per-object bitmask (obj+0x5d), looks up the region's 0x54-byte damage-response block, fires the '~damaged' permutation change via FUN_004f6c60, copies the region's response flags (bits 0x20/0x40/0x80/0x100) into the object's status word/byte, and forwards region effect data via FUN_004f4160.
results.summary: Marks an object region as destroyed, triggers its '~damaged' state change, and propagates the region's damage-response flags onto the object.

results.name: object_regions_reset_permutation_lock
results.evidence: Iterates the object type's region table (count at +0x240, stride 0x54 array at +0x244); for every region flagged 0x10 with more than one permutation (+0x48>1), writes a per-region lock byte at obj+0x180+i derived from the caller-supplied unaff_BL flag.
results.summary: For each multi-permutation region flagged 0x10 on the object's type, writes a per-region lock byte on the object based on a caller flag.

results.name: hash_table_set_or_remove
results.evidence: Classic open hash-table code: bucket = key % capacity, linear search of the bucket's linked list by key; on param_1==-1 the matched node is unlinked and returned to the freelist, otherwise its stored value is updated; grows storage via FUN_004f0620 when the freelist is empty.
results.summary: Generic hash-table helper: removes a key's entry (returning it to the freelist) when the new value is -1, otherwise inserts or updates the key's stored value.

results.name: hash_table_get
results.evidence: Same bucket = key % capacity hashing scheme as hash_table_set_or_remove; walks the bucket's linked list for a matching key and returns its stored value, or -1 if the table is unused or the key is absent. 35 callers, consistent with a generic widely-used lookup helper.
results.summary: Looks up a key in the open hash table shared with hash_table_set_or_remove, returning its stored value or -1 if not found.

results.name: hash_table_grow_freelist
results.evidence: Calls GlobalAlloc twice (an 8-byte header, then a 600-byte node pool), then threads the new pool's 0x3c-byte node slots onto the table's freelist (unaff_ESI+0x10) -- the expansion routine invoked by hash_table_set_or_remove when its freelist is exhausted.
results.summary: Allocates a new block of hash-table node storage via GlobalAlloc and links its slots onto the table's freelist.

results.name: vector3d_barycentric_interpolate
results.evidence: For each of 3 float components computes (C[i]-A[i])*w2 + (D[i]-A[i])*w1 + A[i], the standard barycentric blend of a base point A with two edge points C and D by weights w1/w2.
results.summary: Computes a barycentric-weighted interpolation of a 3D point among a base vector and two edge vectors, given two blend weights.

results.name: bsp_lightmap_sample_vertex_color
results.evidence: For lightmap type 1, decodes packed 16-bit lightmap samples from type-block+0xf8 using the (n*2+1)*1.5259022e-5 dequantization (a 15-bit signed color decode), or for type 0/0xc reads raw float vertex colors (stride 0x38, +0xc); barycentric-interpolates the 3 triangle-vertex samples by (param_2,param_3) and forwards the result to FUN_00524590/FUN_0043f630.
results.summary: Samples and barycentrically interpolates a BSP triangle's lightmap or raw vertex color (handling both quantized and raw-float formats) and forwards it for accumulation.

results.name: bsp_lightmap_sample_vertex_incident
results.evidence: Mirrors bsp_lightmap_sample_vertex_color's dual-format (type 1 vs 0/0xc) triangle lookup but reads the incident/normal-direction float pair at different strides (0x20/0x38), barycentric-interpolates it, and forwards to FUN_00524590 with a different blend constant (0x3e99999a, ~0.3) before FUN_0043f630.
results.summary: Samples and interpolates a BSP triangle's lightmap incident-direction vectors, the companion routine to bsp_lightmap_sample_vertex_color.

results.name: lights_initialize
results.evidence: Matches the cea-pdb hint via the 'lights'/'light' strings; allocates the object-lights data_array with a 0x380-byte stride (FUN_005380d0), updates a CRC checksum for a size-4 field, marks the subsystem-enabled byte, and creates an associated cluster_partition when the allocation succeeds.
results.summary: Initializes the object-lights data_array (0x380-byte element stride) and its associated cluster partition.

results.name: lights_dispose_all
results.evidence: Marks three related data_array headers (the lights table plus two others at DAT_00860b28/DAT_00860b24) for immediate deletion (byte at +0x24=1) and calls data_delete_all on each, and resets a 0x200-entry lookup index array to -1.
results.summary: Tears down the lights data_array and two related tables, deleting all entries in each and resetting a lookup index array.

results.name: light_new_attached
results.evidence: Allocates a light datum via datum_new only when the parent object's type is 'always visible' or already parented (pbVar1&1 or +0xb8!=-1); populates color (param_2), marker indices (param_3/4/5), owner object (param_1), -1 link sentinels (+0x10/+0x58), and a lifetime seeded from DAT_008607c4-1.
results.summary: Allocates and initializes a new attached light record on an object (color, marker bindings, owner, lifetime), only when the object is eligible.

results.name: light_delete
results.evidence: Calls FUN_00552020 (the same render-deregister helper used by object_light_clear_dirty_flag) followed by datum_delete, mirroring the allocation pattern of light_new_attached/light_new_positioned.
results.summary: Deregisters and frees a light datum, undoing light_new_attached/light_new_positioned's allocation.

results.name: light_new_positioned
results.evidence: Like light_new_attached, allocates via datum_new, but stores an explicit world-space position/direction pair (param_4 vector plus unaff_EBX vector) when param_2==-1, or a marker-relative offset otherwise, seeding lifetime from a separate frame counter (DAT_006f1d6c+0xc) rather than DAT_008607c4.
results.summary: Allocates a new light datum positioned either at an explicit world position/direction or relative to a marker, seeding its lifetime from the current tick counter.

results.name: object_lights_update_all
results.evidence: Iterates every active entry in the lights data_array, deletes ones whose lifetime has expired (comparing the current tick DAT_006f1d6c+0xc against each light's duration at +0xf4, via FUN_004d0630/datum_delete), computes attenuated/marker-attached colors for the survivors, and appends up to 0x80 of them into the render queue (DAT_007c1480/DAT_007c1484), continuing into object_lights_update_continue for the remainder.
results.summary: Per-frame update of every active light: expires stale ones, computes their attenuated/attached colors, and appends up to 128 of them to the render queue.

results.name: object_lights_update_continue
results.evidence: Body is essentially byte-identical to the tail of object_lights_update_all (color falloff, marker-attachment lookup, render-queue append via DAT_007c1480/DAT_007c1484); invoked to process the remaining active lights after the first is handled.
results.summary: Continuation of object_lights_update_all's per-light update loop, processing the remaining active lights and appending them to the render queue.

results.name: light_transient_add
results.evidence: Appends a short-lived dynamic light (position from param_1, color/intensity derived from param_4 and the object's type block) into a fixed 8-slot parallel-array table (DAT_008609cc.. stride 0x28, capped by DAT_00860b0c), skipping zero-color entries.
results.summary: Adds a transient per-frame dynamic light entry into a fixed 8-slot table, storing its position, color, and owning-object data.

results.name: light_hash_gather_indices
results.evidence: Walks a hash-bucket chain (DAT_00860b14/DAT_00860b28) collecting up to unaff_SI light-datum ids into the caller's output short array, the same hash-walk pattern seen in object_hash_clear_flag_bit3/object_hash_set_flag_bit3.
results.summary: Collects up to N light-datum indices from a hash-chain into a caller-provided array.

results.name: lights_apply_spot_falloff
results.evidence: For each active light listed in DAT_008607cc, computes cone/spot attenuation from the light's half-angle (type-block+0x14, thresholds 1.5708/0.7854 rad) and forwards the resulting intensity/position to FUN_00552a60, gathering attached-light ids via light_hash_gather_indices when the light shares the object's color flag.
results.summary: Applies spot/cone falloff to each active light based on its half-angle and forwards the resulting intensity and position for rendering.

results.name: lights_apply_spot_falloff_scaled
results.evidence: Near-duplicate of lights_apply_spot_falloff, but additionally multiplies intensity by the type block's brightness field (+0x24) when a 'no scale' status bit is clear, and forwards the result to FUN_00552980 instead of FUN_00552a60.
results.summary: Variant of lights_apply_spot_falloff that also applies a per-type brightness scale before forwarding to a different render sink.

results.name: object_regions_sum_luminance
results.evidence: Sums perceptual luminance (0.299/0.587/0.114 weights) of each visible region's stored vertex color across the object's region table, then recurses into the object's sibling (obj+0x46) and child (obj+0x45) attachment links, accumulating their luminance too.
results.summary: Recursively computes an object's total perceptual-luminance across its own visible regions plus every attached child/sibling object.

results.name: object_sample_ambient_and_dynamic_light
results.evidence: Seeds an output color from a default ambient constant (PTR_DAT_00686b0c), optionally overrides it via a BSP lightmap probe (FUN_00555190) and interpolated static color (bsp_lightmap_sample_vertex_color), adds nearby dynamic-light contributions gathered by object_lights_gather_nearest, and clamps the final result to [0,1].
results.summary: Computes total lighting at a point by combining a default/lightmap ambient sample with nearby dynamic lights, clamped to [0,1].

results.name: object_sample_ambient_color_and_incident
results.evidence: Companion to object_sample_ambient_and_dynamic_light: seeds a color and an incident/normal vector from defaults (PTR_DAT_00686b08), overrides both via the same BSP probe (FUN_00555190) plus bsp_lightmap_sample_vertex_color and bsp_lightmap_sample_vertex_incident, and applies a small +0.1 brightening bias to the color.
results.summary: Samples a point's ambient lightmap color and incident-direction vector, applying a small brightening bias to the color.

results.name: bsp_triangle_sample_color_and_incident
results.evidence: Existing name 'object_cause_damage' does not match the code: it validates a triangle/material via type/frame checks then calls the same FUN_0043f250/FUN_00444550/bsp_lightmap_sample_vertex_color/bsp_lightmap_sample_vertex_incident sequence used by the sibling BSP lighting-sampler functions, applying a +0.1 bias to the sampled color -- no damage is applied anywhere in this function.
results.summary: Samples a BSP triangle's static lightmap color and incident-direction vectors once frame/material validity checks pass; despite its inherited name it performs lighting sampling, not damage application.

results.name: object_sample_ambient_lighting
results.evidence: Probes object_lighting_sample_point at the object's own position plus up to 4 offset points around its bounding radius, accumulating and averaging the resulting position/normal/color fields into a 0x74-byte lighting-sample output struct.
results.summary: Builds an averaged ambient-lighting sample for an object by probing its center and several offset points around its bounding volume.

results.name: object_lights_gather_visible
results.evidence: Iterates a light list via FUN_004f5f70/object_lights_gather_nearest, collecting up to *(param_1+0x40) light-datum indices into the output array at param_1+0x44 and resolving each stored id into a light-record pointer.
results.summary: Gathers the visible/nearby light-datum indices for an object into its light list and resolves each to a light-record pointer.

results.name: object_lighting_sample_point
results.evidence: Casts a BSP occlusion/collision probe (magic id 0xc221, same family as object_damage_apply_line_of_sight's FUN_00505880 call) from up to 4 mirrored directions or a supplied normal, then barycentric-interpolates the hit triangle's lightmap color (bsp_lightmap_sample_vertex_color) and incident vector (bsp_lightmap_sample_vertex_incident) via FUN_004f2ff0.
results.summary: Casts a probe ray from a point (optionally along a supplied normal) against the BSP and returns the interpolated lightmap color and incident direction at the hit point.

results.name: object_light_clear_dirty_flag
results.evidence: For a light datum whose status bit 0x2 (byte at +2) is set, calls FUN_00552020 (the same render-list deregister used in light_delete's teardown path) and clears that bit. Internally named chimera__light_table by the input hints, which is not a real Blam identifier.
results.summary: Deregisters a light datum from the render list and clears its 'queued' status bit when set.

results.name: object_light_update_transform
results.evidence: For a light not yet linked to a marker (+0x58==-1) computes a default orientation basis via FUN_004f6030/FUN_004f6080; otherwise transforms a stored offset through the parent object's node matrix (matrix4x3_transform_point/matrix4x3_transform_normal) and re-orthogonalizes it (vector3d_build_perpendicular/vector3d_normalize_with_length); when the 'needs cone update' status bit is set, also computes and stores a clamped cone angle/direction via FUN_00551f00.
results.summary: Recomputes an attached light's world-space transform (from its marker or a default basis) and, when flagged, its spotlight cone parameters.

results.name: object_lights_refresh_transforms
results.evidence: Iterates every light datum (via FUN_004d0630) and, for each whose transform-dirty status bit (bit 2 of the +2 word) is set, clears the bit and calls object_light_update_transform to recompute it.
results.summary: Sweeps all light datums and recomputes the transform of every one flagged as dirty.

results.name: object_lights_gather_nearest
results.evidence: Walks a spatial hash bucket (DAT_00860b20/DAT_00860b24) of lights near a point, computes distance and a luminance-weighted falloff against each light's radius (+0x54), and keeps the strongest up to param_8 lights in the caller's output arrays (ids in param_4, weights in param_5, falloffs in param_6), replacing the currently-weakest kept entry when a stronger one is found.
results.summary: Finds the strongest nearby lights (by distance-attenuated luminance) around a point from a spatial hash, keeping the top N results in the caller's arrays.
